meta.purpose: Read model for every report the platform must serve. Machine-readable so that Workstream V can derive the index strategy from ACTUAL access patterns rather than from guesses, and so that RLS and PII posture per report is reviewable in one place.
meta.status: DESIGN_ONLY — no view, materialized view or index has been created anywhere

conventions.grain: one row of the report output represents exactly this
conventions.materialization: QUERY = ad hoc; VIEW = named view; MATVIEW = materialized, needs a refresh story
conventions.piiExposure: NONE | PSEUDONYMOUS | CONTACT | FINANCIAL — the strongest class any output column carries
conventions.rls: who may read the report at all; financial and cross-participant reports are operator-only
conventions.settlementRule: every settlement figure is DERIVED from payment_allocations; no report may read a stored settlement value
conventions.rlsRoles: MACHINE-READABLE list of roles permitted to read the report: anon | authenticated | operator | service. Checked by the validator. rlsNotes is human prose and is NEVER pattern-matched — regexing prose produced a false positive on the phrase 'never exposed to anon', and a checker that reads English is a checker that reports noise.
conventions.monetaryMeasures: EXPLICIT list of measures that carry money. Declared, never inferred from the name: a keyword scan for 'total' matched total_points and entries_total and wrongly demanded a currency dimension on three points-based reports. Counts, points and positions are not money, and no regex over English measure names can reliably tell the difference.

meta.indexRedundancyResolved: Two left-prefix redundancies found by the derivation were resolved at the source rather than merely reported: pool_entries(participant_id) folded into (participant_id, pool_id), and pool_entries(pool_id) into (pool_id, deleted_at). Keeping both members of a prefix pair pays write cost twice for one read path.

reports.name: participant_history
reports.question: Everything this participant has ever done on the platform.
reports.grain: one row per (participant, pool_entry) per currency
filters: canonical identity resolved first (a superseded id must return the surviving identity's history)
reports.notes: MUST resolve canonical identity before filtering, or a merged participant's history appears empty. This is the most likely reporting bug in the whole set. Grain includes currency: a money aggregate without it would sum across currencies, which the financial engine refuses as wrong rather than approximate.
reports.rlsNotes: operator; a participant-facing variant must be a separate projection restricted to their own canonical id

reports.name: pool_participation
reports.question: Who is in this pool, and what is each entry's standing?
reports.grain: one row per pool_entry per currency
reports.notes: Soft-deleted entries must be excluded by default — a withdrawn entry appearing in a pool list has previously been reported as a live bug class. Grain includes currency because expected_fee and allocated are money.
reports.rlsNotes: operator; public variant exposes display_name only, never email

reports.name: competition_history
reports.question: Every edition of a competition and its pools.
reports.grain: one row per (competition_edition, pool) per currency
reports.notes: distinct_participant_count must count CANONICAL participants, otherwise a pre-merge duplicate inflates the headline number. Grain includes currency: a money aggregate without it would sum across currencies, which the financial engine refuses as wrong rather than approximate.
reports.rlsNotes: operator; safe to expose as an aggregate public projection

reports.name: multiple_entries
reports.question: Which participants hold more than one entry in the same pool?
reports.grain: one row per (participant, pool) with entry_count > 1
reports.notes: Multiple entries are LEGITIMATE (this is why there is no unique constraint on (participant, pool) — see the M-3 supersession). This report is for review, not for enforcement. Rule DQ-ST-04 catches the accidental case: same label.

reports.name: payment_history
reports.question: Every payment recorded, by whom, how, and when.
reports.notes: external_reference must NOT appear in any shared export. Legacy rows have amount IS NULL (LEGACY_ASSERTED); the report must render that as 'asserted, amount unknown', never as 0 — rendering it as 0 would understate cash collected.
reports.rlsNotes: operator ONLY — never exposed to anon or authenticated

reports.name: payment_allocations
reports.question: How was each payment split across entries?
reports.notes: This report is the audit trail for one payment funding several entries. Currency must match payment and entry (DQ-FN-05); a mismatch is a data defect, not a display issue.

reports.name: unpaid_balances
reports.question: Which entries have received nothing?
reports.grain: one row per pool_entry with settlement = UNPAID
reports.notes: LEGACY_ASSERTED entries must be EXCLUDED from this report and reported separately (R-07b concern). Chasing a participant who paid years ago for a payment nobody recorded is a real-world harm this report can cause.

reports.name: partial_balances
reports.question: Which entries are partially funded?
reports.grain: one row per pool_entry with settlement = PARTIALLY_PAID
reports.notes: shortfall = expected - allocated, exact decimal. Never computed in the client.

reports.name: overpayments
reports.question: Which entries received more than their fee, and which payments have an unapplied balance?
reports.grain: one row per pool_entry with settlement = OVERPAID, plus one row per payment with unapplied > 0
reports.notes: OVERPAID is a reportable state, not an error — there is deliberately no cap of allocation against expected fee. An unapplied balance is money held and owed: this report is how it stops being forgotten.

reports.name: prizes_and_winnings
reports.question: Who won what, in which pool, under which rule version?
reports.notes: prize_allocations.participant_id is denormalised for this report; DQ-FN-10 asserts it agrees with the entry, or winnings get attributed to the wrong person.
reports.rlsNotes: operator; a public projection may show display_name + rank + gross, never payment state

reports.name: participant_net_position
reports.question: Across everything, is this participant up or down?
reports.grain: one row per participant per currency
reports.notes: Grain is PER CURRENCY, deliberately: summing across currencies is the cross-currency error the financial engine refuses. A single 'net' number across currencies would be meaningless even when USD is the only value present.

reports.name: competition_performance
reports.question: How did each entry score in a competition edition?
reports.refresh: on result recorded, and on demand; never on a timer alone — a stale leaderboard after a result is a visible incorrectness
reports.notes: Scoring is computed by the app's own scoring logic, NOT reimplemented in SQL. Workstream N exists to guarantee no migration changes any of these numbers. A SQL reimplementation would be a second source of truth for money.
reports.rlsNotes: operator; public projection is the published ranking only

reports.name: ranking_history
reports.question: How did the leaderboard change over time?
reports.notes: position_delta must be computed against a STABLE BASELINE snapshot, not merely the previous row — the BR2026 rule that club movement and participant movement are distinct concepts applies here. Snapshots are never re-pointed after an identity merge (see IDENTITY_MODEL §6): this report shows history as published.

reports.name: year_over_year_participation
reports.question: Is participation growing, and who returns?
reports.refresh: nightly; a day-stale participation trend has no decision attached to it
reports.notes: 'Returning' is meaningless without canonical identity resolution — an unmerged duplicate reads as a NEW participant every season, which would systematically overstate growth and understate retention. This report is the strongest business argument for Workstream C.
reports.rlsNotes: operator; aggregate-only public projection is safe

reports.name: pool_financial_reconciliation
reports.question: For this pool: expected, collected, outstanding, awarded, net.
reports.notes: Mirrors poolReconciliation() in financial.mjs exactly; if the two ever disagree, that is a finding. legacy_asserted_entry_count is shown BESIDE the money, never folded into it: those entries have no recoverable amount, so any total that silently includes them is wrong.

reports.name: audit_history
reports.question: What happened, when, by whom, and does the chain verify?
reports.notes: safe_metadata carries no names, emails, phones or payment references (B1/ADR-008, enforced by DQ-AU-01). chain_verified comes from recomputing the hash chain (DQ-AU-02): an audit log that advertises tamper evidence and cannot verify is worse than none.

reports.name: operational_health
reports.question: Is the provider snapshot fresh, and is the outbox delivering?
reports.grain: one row per (sync_state) plus one row per outbox status bucket
reports.notes: This is the report that turns the platform's worst failure mode — a silently stale provider snapshot, which produces NO signal at all — into something observable. dead_count > 0 means a notification was lost and needs triage, so it must alert rather than merely display.
reports.rlsNotes: operator; safe as a service-role health endpoint
